title: 26th sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim (Dhiggaru) chaired the middle session
summary: The sitting opened with question time, where MPs pressed the Housing Minister on when Gulhifalhu plots and 4,000 Hulhumale' Phase 2 flats will be handed over; the exchange became heated, several points of order were raised, and the chair named four members and asked them to leave the chamber before suspending the sitting. After the break the Deputy Speaker chaired the first readings of two government bills and the continued debate on the Insurance Bill, which was accepted for consideration 77-0 and sent to the Finance Committee. The opening attendance figure is garbled in the text, so it is left blank.

items.title: Opening prayer and start of the sitting
Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 2 members on leave, 3 on official travel

items.title: Question to the Minister of Housing, Land and Urban Development on Gulhifalhu plots, Hulhumale' flats and related housing issues
items.outcome: answered; follow-up questions from many members; sitting suspended after the chair asked four members to leave

items.title: Bill on planning and running the built environment (first reading)
Bill to amend the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010) (first reading)
Unfinished business: debate on the Insurance Bill
Vote on accepting the Insurance Bill
items.outcome: passed 77-0; sent to the Finance Committee

speakers.name: Ali Haidar Ahmed
positions: As Housing Minister, said no firm date can be set for Gulhifalhu plots as reclamation and bridge works continue.
Said ACC-reviewed flat applications will be re-reviewed under common criteria before handover, with a final list from the ministry.
Said the government aims to build 85,000 housing units this term; promised written answers where information was missing.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Raised points of order saying the minister should answer questions directly rather than make remarks.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked why plot lists are not reviewed like flat lists and whether any housing project has started.
Raised points of order saying his second question had gone unanswered.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked what action is taken against people who obtained social-housing flats by deception and rent them out.
In the Insurance Bill debate, said safari vessels and dhonis should be insurable and banks should lend against them.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when Gulhifalhu plot winners, earlier-scheme plot holders and the 4,000 Hulhumale' Phase 2 flat winners will get their allocations.
Said residents will wait for the dates given and question again if they are not met.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked how many housing units the government plans to start this year and next year.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Asked when water, sewerage and power will reach the 100 housing units built in Vilufushi and when they will be handed over.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: As sponsor, presented the Insurance Bill to regulate insurance companies and criticised opposition conduct that morning.
Said plots given on sea and lagoon cannot be insured.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Backed the bill and said land given from the sea should be insurable.
Said Maldives had insurance companies since 1985 without a law and the bill is needed.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked whether the minister would deliver plots and flats without changing the stand or any citizen's rights.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether the minister was acting on the President's instruction or his own decision in halting plot and flat allocations.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked why flat agreements are delayed for applicants the ACC review found eligible or with only minor issues.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked how many people were asked to give up plots on sea-based land and whether 100 flats for customs staff will proceed.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Questioned whether plot documents on reef areas reflect reality, saying the sites lack space for schools or roads.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill, saying insurance provides protection and that large risks are currently insured abroad.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said plots and flats already issued should be reviewed so they can be insured under proper rules.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, urged expert input at committee stage and criticised opposition conduct and earlier plot allocations.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the bill, including a licensing regulator, and urged committee consultation with experts.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Regretted the disruption of the minister's answers and said unregistered plots cannot be insured.

decisions: Insurance Bill (sponsor Ahmed Thariq, Mahibadhoo) accepted for consideration 77-0 and sent to the Finance Committee.
First readings of two government bills (built environment planning bill; Decentralization Act amendment) read out.
Chair named four members during question time and asked them to leave the chamber before suspending the sitting.
Next sitting set for 13 August 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Insurance Bill for consideration
